title: Sub-kilometre feasibility Phase 4: adding wave Stokes drift
scope: Currents, fixed 3 percent windage and reanalysis surface Stokes drift versus the same run without Stokes drift, on identical cases.
summary: Adding Stokes drift made no material difference at 6 and 12 h (median change -0.24 and +0.04 km) and made errors worse at 24 and 48 h (median change +0.80 km on 155 cases and +4.98 km on 133 cases). At 48 h the waves composite scored 30.89 km versus 30.87 km for persistence.

limitations: All four tracks are one July-August 2018 deployment episode near Puerto Rico; rolling cases overlap heavily, so case counts are not independent samples.
Forcing is retrospective reanalysis (daily-mean currents, hourly reanalysis wind), not an as-issued forecast.
No 500 m or sub-kilometre positional skill and no St Kitts validation is claimed; final claims require another deployment.
Provider track metadata has unresolved caveats, so no period is treated as confirmed.
The 3 percent windage was not re-estimated after adding Stokes drift, so part of it may already absorb wave drift.
